ana: onboarding NyxLite-7B int4. quick rouge drop on summarization + a weird repeating noun pattern. logs below. anyone seen this with token normalization? :thinking:

leo: paste eval + quant profile

ana: ran `./onboard nyxlite --quant int4` then `pytest tests/summaries.py::smoke_nyxlite`

log snippets:
```
LOAD NyxLite-7B
APPLY QUANT: int4-approx
TOKENIZER: nfkc normalization applied -> combined ligatures
EVAL: ROUGE-L 0.47 (fp16 baseline 0.62)
EVAL: avg_logprob -2.10 (baseline -1.28)
SAMPLE: repeated noun: "company company"
```

dave: nfkc can merge ligatures and change token id ordering. if our rotary lookup assumes token-id contiguous blocks (used in some converters) that could shift sin/cos pairing. is the converted vocab reorder large?

ana: diff shows ~30 indices moved where ligatures were merged. fp16 run unaffected. int4 noisy. repro gist: https://internal/nyx-int4-repro

leo: try forcing tokenizer to keep old splitting (disable nfkc) and re-run int4 with rotary_scale=1.0 (was auto 0.82). also run kvcache sanity check.

ci-bot: scheduled job: `nyxlite-int4-repro-try2` started

ci-bot: result: ROUGE-L 0.59, avg_logprob -1.34, repetition resolved. :white_check_mark:

dave: conclusion: token-normalization-induced id permutations break rotary index assumptions in quantized runtimes. short-term: pin tokenizer normalization in converter and add `rotary_permutation_check` to conversion CI. long-term: move rotary base away from token-id layout.

ana: created ticket ML-4021 "NyxLite int4: token-normalization reorder -> rotary misalign". adding checklist entry and S3 path for diffs s3://rdw-onboard/nyxlite/int4-diffs/

leo: i'll add a unit test that permutes vocab indices and runs a rotary-phase consistency assert. path: eng-ml/tests/test_rotary_perm.py

ana: thanks — re-run full eval overnight and will update manifest with `tokenizer_nfkc_pinned: true`.
